brief.acceptance:
Add a per-machine runtime catalogue. Shape `runtimes@v0`, a YAML file
at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/interlock/runtimes.yaml` (default
`~/.config/interlock/runtimes.yaml`), path overridable by the
environment variable `INTERLOCK_RUNTIMES` so tests never touch the real
file. Each entry is a named profile: `kind` (the agent CLI herdr
starts, with today's `runtime.kind` semantics), `args` (opaque to
interlock), `model` (a declared label kept for the record, never
parsed), and optional `startup_answers` and `startup_timeout_ms` with
today's semantics. The file is machine truth and is never committed.
`runtimes.example.yaml` in the repository documents the shape with
placeholder entries only and names no vendor.

The existing `runtime:` block in local.yaml keeps working unchanged as
the implicit profile named `default`. local.yaml gains an optional
`default_runtime: <name>`, additive within local@v0; readers accept its
absence forever. An absent catalogue is an empty catalogue, never an
error. A malformed entry refuses with a sentence through the
established readable-refusal surface, naming the nearest vocabulary
term (I3). No PATH probing and no vendor knowledge in code: whether a
profile can start is learned from attempts, never guessed (I6).

Add `interlock runtime list`: name, kind, declared model, and where
the profile came from (catalogue or local.yaml). A JSON Schema
`schemas/runtimes@v0.json` and `interlock schema validate` cover the
new shape. Strict TypeScript, no assertions, no non-null operators.
Tests pin: a valid catalogue parses; a malformed one refuses with a
sentence; an absent one is empty; the legacy `runtime:` block still
resolves as `default`; the list renders. Preserve every historical
brief, debrief, note and receipt. Append typed notes for choices and
surprises. Run the focused test files and lint before handoff. No
push, no merge, no deployment; the human merges.

decisions.what: Extracted the herdr agent-name compliance pattern (the regex behind isCompliantAgentName) out of packages/runner/src/herdr/adapter.ts into a new packages/runner/src/agentName.ts, re-exported from the herdr adapter so every existing import site is unchanged.
decisions.because: The brief requires a runtime catalogue name to match "the same shape herdr accepts for an agent name". That predicate was private to the herdr adapter file. Importing herdr/adapter.ts directly into a runtime-agnostic catalogue reader would pull in herdr socket and agent-kind knowledge alongside it, which reads like the cross-adapter leak I6 exists to prevent; the name-shape regex itself is not herdr-specific, so it belongs in a module both the herdr adapter and the catalogue reader can depend on without either depending on the other.
decisions.rejected: Duplicating the regex verbatim in runtimeCatalogue.ts: the brief states the two name shapes are "the same", so composing one predicate keeps that guarantee true by construction instead of by two files staying in sync by convention.

decisions.what: Generalized localConfig.ts's private startup-answer parser into an exported parseStartupAnswers(value, fieldPath) in startupAnswers.ts, returning Result<StartupAnswer[], string> (a bare reason, not a LocalConfigRefusal); localConfig.ts now wraps that reason into its own {kind:"malformed", path, reason}. isStringArray moved from a private helper in localConfig.ts to an exported helper in validate.ts so both readers share it too.
decisions.because: The brief says the catalogue reader "reuses its startup-answer validation from packages/runner/src/startupAnswers.ts", but the parser lived in localConfig.ts typed to return a LocalConfigRefusal, the wrong error type for a catalogue entry (RuntimeCatalogueRefusal). Parameterizing on the field path (e.g. "runtime.startup_answers" vs. "runtimes.fast.startup_answers") lets both readers reuse one validator and still produce entry-appropriate sentences.

decisions.what: Built packages/runner/src/runtimeCatalogue.ts's reading half: RUNTIME_CATALOGUE_SHAPE ("runtimes@v0"), CatalogueRuntime (kind, args, model, startupAnswers, startupTimeoutMs), runtimeCataloguePath() (INTERLOCK_RUNTIMES, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/interlock/runtimes.yaml, else ~/.config/interlock/runtimes.yaml), and loadRuntimeCatalogue(path), which treats an absent file as an empty catalogue and refuses a present-but-malformed one with a sentence naming the path, the entry and the field. Entry names are validated against isCompliantAgentName; unknown entry keys, a missing kind/model, and a non-positive startup_timeout_ms all refuse.
decisions.because: "An absent catalogue is an empty catalogue, never an error" (I3-style readable refusal otherwise) is pinned acceptance. loadRuntimeCatalogue(path) takes an explicit path with a default computed by runtimeCataloguePath(), mirroring loadLocalConfig(repoRoot)'s own internal path derivation; most unit tests can then pass an explicit temp path and skip environment-variable stubbing entirely, and only INTERLOCK_RUNTIMES/XDG_CONFIG_HOME so tests never touch the real file.

decisions.what: Named the merged catalogue-or-local runtime entry ResolvedRuntime, not Runtime, and built mergeRuntimes(catalogue, local): local.yaml's runtime: block becomes the entry named "default" (source "local.yaml"), refusing with {kind:"duplicate-default"} if the catalogue also declares "default"; local.yaml gained an optional default_runtime field, checked against the merged set and refusing with {kind:"unknown-default-runtime", name, known} by name, never picked silently. mergeRuntimes takes local as LocalConfig | undefined; the CLI caller collapses a "missing" local.yaml refusal to undefined while still propagating a "malformed" one as a hard refusal.
decisions.because: packages/runner/src/runtime.ts already exports an interface named Runtime for the pane-driving adapter contract, an unrelated concept; ResolvedRuntime says what the value is (the entry resolved from either source) without claiming a vocabulary word that already names a different type in the same package. Treating a missing local.yaml as "no legacy runtime block" (rather than an error) keeps "interlock runtime list" usable in a repository that has a catalogue and no local.yaml yet, while a present-but-broken local.yaml still surfaces as a readable refusal instead of being silently swallowed.

decisions.what: Added the "runtime" command group with a "list" action (packages/cli/src/runtime/list.ts, wired into main.ts) that resolves the repository root exactly as graph show and session show do, loads the catalogue and local.yaml, merges them, and prints one line per runtime as "<name> — kind <kind>, model <model|(none)>, source <catalogue|local.yaml>"; an empty merged view prints one sentence instead. Every refusal (catalogue, local.yaml, merge) renders through its own explain function and exits non-zero.
decisions.because: The acceptance names exactly these four fields (name, kind, declared model, source) and "the list renders" as pinned behavior. The read-first brief says to resolve the repository root and render plain text the way graph show and session show already do; reusing that exact pattern (findRepoRoot, then a plain-text CommandResult) keeps this command unsurprising next to its siblings rather than inventing a second rendering convention.

decisions.what: Added schemas/runtimes@v0.json (permissive additionalProperties, matching local@v0.json's own leniency: the schema documents shape for `interlock schema validate`, while runtimeCatalogue.ts's reader is the strict source of truth), registered automatically by the existing directory-scanning registry with no registry code changes. Added runtimes.example.yaml at the repository root with placeholder names ("fast", "careful") and a placeholder kind ("<agent-cli>"), wired into packages/schemas/src/reference/corpus.ts's referenceSources so docs/shapes.md carries a validated example, then regenerated docs/shapes.md via `interlock schema reference`.
decisions.because: The brief requires the shape covered by both `interlock schema validate` and `schema reference`, and the registry already auto-discovers every schemas/*.json file by title, so no registry or CLI schema-command code needed to change. Matching local@v0.json's permissive-schema-strict-reader split keeps the two enforcement layers consistent across every artifact in this repository rather than inventing a stricter convention for just this one shape.
